sections.category: Micron's AI-memory quarter quadruples revenue and reports HBM sold out through 2026 under $100B of take-or-pay contracts

bullets.body: Micron reported fiscal-Q3-2026 results on June 25 that turn the AI buildout into a memory-supply story: revenue of $41.46 billion, up roughly 346% from $9.30 billion a year earlier and well ahead of the ~$35.25 billion consensus, the company's fifth consecutive record quarter, with Q4 guided to about $50 billion against ~$44 billion expected (versus just over $11 billion in the year-ago quarter). The structural signal is on the high-bandwidth-memory side that feeds Nvidia and AMD accelerators: CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said Micron can fill only half to two-thirds of HBM demand and that all of 2026's supply is already sold out under multi-year contracts, HBM4 revenue has crossed $1 billion and is ramping about twice as fast as the prior HBM3E generation, and the quarter included 16 take-or-pay Strategic Customer Agreements locking in roughly $100 billion of minimum contracted revenue plus $22 billion of upfront customer cash. The read-through is that AI compute is now memory-gated, not just GPU-gated, and that the chip vendors' supply chains are being pre-committed years out. sections.category: Qualcomm names Meta as its first data-center CPU customer and lays out a Dragonfly accelerator roadmap aimed at Nvidia's inference economics

bullets.body: On June 24 Qualcomm unveiled a full data-center roadmap that for the first time attaches a named hyperscaler to its server-silicon push: a strategic, multi-generation agreement under which Meta plans to use the Qualcomm Dragonfly C1000 CPU to power its next-generation server fleet when the part reaches commercial availability in 2028. The roadmap spans the Dragonfly C1000 CPU (claimed >2x better performance-per-watt than existing server CPUs), the Dragonfly AI300 inference accelerator (claimed 4x-8x better performance-per-watt than current GPU-based architectures, sampling 2028), and a new High Bandwidth Compute memory tier Qualcomm says delivers up to a 54x bandwidth jump over its AI200 and ~6x bandwidth-per-watt versus HBM, with 35+ ecosystem partners including Lenovo, Supermicro, Micron, SK hynix and Samsung. The positioning is explicitly an inference-economics attack on Nvidia rather than a training play, and it slots alongside Qualcomm's prior move on a cross-vendor inference compiler to assemble a CPU-plus-accelerator-plus-named-customer stack; the gap is timeline, with first commercial sampling and availability still two years out. sections.category: Gartner puts agent software at $206.5B for 2026 as a $1.5B Indian sovereign-AI unicorn shows where the spend is pooling

bullets.body: Two threads from the corporate side this week sharpen where agentic-AI money is flowing. On the demand side, Gartner's latest forecast pegs AI-agent software spending at about $206.5 billion in 2026 — up roughly 139% from $86.4 billion in 2025 and on track for $376.3 billion in 2027 — a growth rate nearly triple the 47% expansion of overall AI spend, making purpose-built agent software the fastest-growing slice of enterprise software even inside an already-booming market (Gartner pairs the optimism with a standing caution that it expects over 40% of agentic-AI projects to be cancelled by end-2027). On the supply side, the sovereign-AI thesis got a concrete data point: HCLTech confirmed it led a $234 million first close of Sarvam's $300 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation — HCLTech's own $150 million check taking a ~10.5% stake — minting India's newest AI unicorn and funding compute and training for a frontier model targeting coding, agentic and cybersecurity workloads built, hosted and governed inside the country. The pairing shows the agent-spend wave is now pulling national-champion model builders, not just US frontier labs, into the capital flow. sections.category: AI events to plan around now: the AI Engineer World's Fair main program opens today, with summer and fall chip and security dates locked in

bullets.body: The forward calendar across all three sub-tracks. Mainstream dev/data: the AI Engineer World's Fair main program runs June 29 through July 2 at Moscone West in San Francisco (reported at ~29 tracks, ~300 speakers, 6,000+ attendees), opening today with the Coding Agents keynote and the expo, then Autoresearch (July 1) and Harness Engineering (July 2) keynotes across ~12 parallel tracks each; further out, GitHub Universe returns October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. AI-security: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay; Black Hat USA 2026 brings its AI Summit plus the main Briefings at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas in early August, with DEF CON 34 and its AI Village the same week; OWASP Global AppSec USA is November 5-6 in San Francisco; and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series continues to additional cities after its San Francisco stop, so it stays on the watch list. AI-chip/hardware: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is July 22-23 at Moscone (keynote and Instinct MI400-series focus on July 23), Hot Chips 2026 runs August 23-25 at Stanford's Memorial Auditorium, and the AI Infra Summit is September 15-17 at the Santa Clara Convention Center.
